items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: See, my wife does all... All she does is missionary work for her church in El Paso.

ctx.x: That's their kicks, man. But they can't come over here smoking over there. Yeah. Smoking over there, they don't bother them. Yeah, you see. But you can't come across the line. And he was in Los Angeles, you see. And it was hot behind that. There you see. That was in the 39 and 40. He sure was a fine trumpet player. He come after Bob. Fine. Yeah, yeah, yeah, he was. Come after you. Yeah. And that other little drunken boy after Eddie. He sure hated to leave. He said got his ticket. So we had, we had Dorothy played…

Yeah, he was a son. That's what I tell any musician. You don't need no, you don't need no, no pep. You don't need no kind of pep. Marijuana to... To give your pep to play. You don't need it. Heroin, like some of the big shots used that we don't know nothing about. Yeah, you don't need it. Or liquor, you don't need it. See, now I'm talking from the actual experience. That's by far... I tried to tell... By far your greatest teacher. That's more than you can ever learn in any book that you read. Wow. Your actual…
Yeah, yeah. You never had drunk in your life? A little high, you know. But seeing this drunk,
